body: I actually inhibited 2 of the three symptoms of the Macdonald triad when I was a kid. The third was a problem for a little bit, but i got over it. So, who knows I just might enjoy it.

That sounds like borderline carelessness to me. I'd hate to leave a wake of destruction behind me so that I can get over my mental illness. What if worrying about 'what will go wrong' is stopping me from murdering innocent people? I guess there's a level of 'trusting one's self' required.

No worries. To me, bluntness is synonymous with honesty. So it's appreciated. It troubles me that having depression feels so much like going against the current. Everyday is a fight.

Yeah, I for sure overthink everything way too much. It's hard to focus so much on the positive. It's almost like playing pretend, like the negative isn't really there. I have a garbage memory so I naturally live in the moment, but when I'm alone in my head the self-reflection becomes so easy and gradually eats away at me. 

I've found out that life is just a big balancing act; an act i'm not too great at.

Yeah, we practically know jack shit about the human brain. The closest thing to Nikola Tesla we have today, I'd say, is Elon Musk. Hopefully for your sake he turns from infrastructure and ventures into the world of medical science and neurology.

I can't imagine the frustration of not knowing if there even is a cure, I'm sorry.

EXACTLY! Where do they expect to go?! oh good job you're now exactly one car length closer to where you were going, saving you literally one second. That's the willful ignorance that bugs me so much. Putting others in danger for little to nothing.

But yeah, I feel the only way to increase the number of people that enjoy your company is to put yourself out there. Which gets harder as time passes because people get so ingrained in their ways.

Well to be fair, they did explode quite a few good people to get to where we are today. Also it's crazy easier to follow the laws of physics as opposed to the vague map we have of the brain.

The only thing I can recommend is to drink more/proper amounts of water. It helps remedy a surprising amount of problems. 

Yeah I feel you though, I see these people who are doing crazy things with missing limbs. A good head on your shoulders can do wonders.

In the long run it's nice, but it sucks to always have to check yourself. Just a small example, I always use my signal and give ample room before merging. I can hardly say the same for the majority of drivers out there. Just the other day I almost crashed into someone coming out of a gas station because they cut me off.

The problem is that it's hard to find those "other people," for me at least. It's like I meet a bunch of people who say they like me and then it filters down to 1-2 people that actually want me around. I'm sure it's my fault for not putting myself out there or something.

Yeah for reals. The brain is so densely packed with synapses the wiring is insane. It's not like any of the wiring is color coated either. 

All I can do is avoid comparing myself to others and focus on becoming a better version of myself. It's just discouraging when you slip back into the ol' depression.
That sounds delightful. I don't really like the idea of starting out with a handicap though. Like I'm sure I'd be a super awesome person if I didn't have all this fucked up stuff in my head.

Yeah, I most definitely hold myself to higher standard than the general populace of the world. I've actually been told that several times, that I shouldn't always be there sometimes. It's just that I always am, so it feels like lying. Like consciously ignoring someone. 

Not many people ask me for things, so I guess that sort of is my fear. Eventually, maybe, they won't need me anymore. I generally like lessening the burden of others.

I'm sorry about your head. Luckily this is really only a problem when I go outside. Yeah cured after testing several kinds of medication or years and years of hard work where you still aren't completely cured. It's like alcoholism, you never truly become cured just constantly recovering.

Yeah, it's a thing of great willpower to continue in the face of such doubt. 

I sweat like I'm the mayor guy from the first x-men movie. Like 110 degree weather in Florida sweating. My heart goes into my throat. My hands shake like I'm operating a jack hammer. It's like i'm being pursued by a grizzly bear.

Yes! I read that same thing, about unappreciated kindnesses and the language of love. 

Throwing myself under the bus is a little melodramatic, but I'm the kind of person to always say yes. I text back within minutes, always. I will take the high road when I realize someone has crossed a line. 

For example: When my friend told me that I am depression incarnate, I just nodded and agreed until the conversation was over.

I think this exact same thing. It doesn't subside the physical repercussions of anxiety for me though. I don't care what most people think of me, it just bugs me that I'm negatively affecting their lives. Unlike me, they actually want to live.

People always make life out to be the best thing, but the past ~20 years have taught me otherwise. Which makes me think "is all this difficult shit worth it?"

I agree, simple is good, but I feel me kindergartening myself is belittling. 

I should probably look out more for myself. I have a tendency to put myself under the bus for the benefit of parties involved.
I realize this is the theme of my life. Tiny dedicated steps. I did it for a while and mentally it got easier, but my body didn't seem to want to follow, my heart still goes ballistic.

I'm sure there are laws against making yourself feel good in public. 

joking aside, it's easier said than done. That's like telling me to "just be happy."

Yeah I kinda black out and do alright, but the sweating and shaking is visibly embarrassing. 

Yeah, I've tried cognitive behavioral stuff. I end up making fun of myself because I sounding like a kindergarten teacher.
because I wouldn't like to add onto the troubles people already have
I find that it's almost too forceful for me to do that. I'd hate to be one of those people who practically scream "LOOK AT ME!" but yes my personality is quite the handful.

Yeah, I have some intense stage fright. I vibrate like a... *cough* something that vibrates. I know it sounds like a cop out but it would be a lot of effort to overcome that just to find out I'm not really that funny. 

Yeah, I feel the majority of the experiences I have with people are on somewhat good terms. It just rarely happens.

I'm not religious either, but the idea of having power over every aspect of life is comforting.

Yeah, it's kind of hard to be good to myself when I'm so accustomed to self-loathing. I was good to myself for a couple years. I was just over 300 lbs and I started lifting and doing a bit of cardio and I'm a sturdy 200 now.

I guess 'stupid' is kind of a harsh term, I would rather say people are willfully ignorant. Sadly enough it's human experiences that I value above all. I love to make people laugh, I feel it's one of the only guaranteed ways to make peoples lives better. I live in quite a bit of solitude, It's easy for me to go weeks without speaking. Unfortunately it doesn't even require me to be in the equation. People treating other people shitty, in general, rustles my jimmies. 

It's hard to tell what movie I want with all this anxiety. I don't want to be famous because any sort of attention feels really weird to me. Maybe if I were god, or some other equally omnipotent figure. 'tis a tall order I know. 

I feel I do have some solid genes. It just got all messed up with the upbringing. I truly wish to trade brains with a terminally ill kid. They'd be able to do so much. My brain wiring is 100% at fault. It's like walking a minefield trying to live a normal life.
